canonical_statement: For every commutative ring R, if R is Noetherian, then the univariate polynomial ring R[X] is Noetherian.

canonical_formal_target.fully_explicit_expression: ∀ {R : Type u} [inst : CommRing.{u} R] [@IsNoetherianRing.{u} R (@CommSemiring.toSemiring.{u} R (@CommRing.toCommSemiring.{u} R inst))], @IsNoetherianRing.{u} (@Polynomial.{u} R (@CommSemiring.toSemiring.{u} R (@CommRing.toCommSemiring.{u} R inst))) (@Polynomial.semiring.{u} R (@CommSemiring.toSemiring.{u} R (@CommRing.toCommSemiring.{u} R inst)))

domain_and_universes: R is an arbitrary implicit Type u carrying CommRing and IsNoetherianRing instances; Polynomial R is in the same universe; no Nontrivial, characteristic, domain, or field premise is present.
hypotheses: R has a commutative ring structure
conclusion: The univariate polynomial ring Polynomial R is Noetherian.
minimal_import_basis: Polynomial.Basic supplies the polynomial carrier and CommRing instance; Noetherian.Defs supplies IsNoetherianRing, ideal finite generation, and their iff. Deleting either import fails, while the proof-bearing Mathlib.RingTheory.Polynomial.Basic module is deliberately not imported.

checked_alternate_encodings.boundary: Directly expands Noetherianity to finite generation of every ideal for both the coefficient and polynomial rings.

uncredited_alternate_encodings: ascending-chain or well-founded-order formulations without a separately checked transport
finite-variable MvPolynomial and general finite-type algebra strengthenings

included: the zero ring and all subsingleton commutative Noetherian rings
fields, domains, finite rings, and PIDs only as special cases of the general domain
